one_month_reasoning: No Oracle earnings in the window: Q2 FY27 results are set for 2026-12-14, after 2026-11-04. In the window: (1) the $0.50 dividend goes ex around the Oct 9 record date (paid Oct 23), which mechanically lowers the median by ~$0.50 (Q1 FY27 release). (2) The Investor Day management told analysts to 'mark your calendars' for in October (Q1 FY27 call). No exact date is confirmed; AI World runs Oct 25-28. Last year's analyst day set FY30 targets, so this is a guidance event: possible FCF-positive date (CFO: 'we have not given a particular time frame on that yet'), AI-infrastructure gross margins ('flatten' after ramp), FY28 capex. It is two-sided: a dated FCF turn would help; a higher FY28 capex plan or a reiteration of no date would hurt. (3) Big-4 hyperscaler Q3 results in late October with first 2027 capex guides, mildly positive per the standing capex view. (4) FOMC Oct 27-28; OpenAI funding/IPO news; Jupiter project-loan and CDS headlines. No clean drift signal (the stock fell after a beat-and-raise quarter paired with the $20B ATM). So: lognormal centred at ~$142.9 (spot less dividend) with monthly sigma ~0.165 (56%/3.5 = 0.16, widened slightly for the Investor Day), and a touch of extra tail at both ends.

fair_value.method: Blend at 2027-10-05: P/E 0.45 (NTM non-GAAP EPS $11.0, ~12% below consensus-implied ~$12.5, x 15x = $165), SOTP 0.35 (legacy software 15x after-tax earnings $264B + OCI 3.2x NTM sales $285B, less ~$140B net debt excluding operating leases, / 3.15B shares = $130), EV/EBITDA 0.20 ($77B haircut NTM EBITDA x 10x, less $140B, / 3.15B = $200). Blended = $160.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 = 8/12 x FY28 $10.2 + 4/12 x FY29 $12.6 = $11.0 (consensus-implied NTM ~$12.5, so a ~12% haircut); multiple 15x vs peer CY2027 median 21.5x (range 8.5-27.0x)

inputs_detail.derivation: Company guide on the Q1 FY27 call; Yahoo consensus $8.14 (37 analysts) as a cross-check

Yahoo FY28 consensus $11.00, marked ~7% lower. Share count rose to 3.024B after the $19.9B Q1 ATM sale (10-Q), and the FY27-28 'peak capex' plan with consensus FCF of -$32.6B in FY28 (MarketScreener) implies more equity or debt. Depreciation is up 134% y/y and AI gross margin is falling (call), so I put EPS near the lower-middle of the range. The $9.14 Zacks FY28 figure is a GAAP-like basis (FY27 $6.69 on that basis) and is not used.

No non-GAAP FY29 consensus is published. Consensus-implied is ~$15.4 (Zacks GAAP-basis FY29/FY28 ratio 12.84/9.14 = 1.40 applied to $11.00, per the supervisor; my own MarketScreener ratio of 1.47 gives ~$16.2, so the supervisor figure is if anything conservative). I assume +24% from my $10.2 FY28 instead: OCI ramp gross margins are thin, depreciation is +134% y/y and $20-40B more financing is likely in Jan-May 2027. This is my judgment, ~18% below the street, not consensus.

Reconciled 10-peer CY2027 median 21.5x (hyperscaler sub-median 23.7x, enterprise-software sub-median 15.6x). 15x sits inside the range between CRM 14.3x and IBM 16.8x and essentially at the software sub-median. The ~30% discount to the overall median is argued as persistent through Oct-2027 on company facts: management calls FY27-28 peak capex years with no FCF-positive date ('we have not given a particular time frame', Q1 call), so FCF stays negative through May 2028; S&P BBB- (stable) and Moody's Baa2 (negative), while hyperscaler peers are A or better; S&P puts ~half the $664B RPO with OpenAI; another $20-40B of debt/equity is likely in Jan-May 2027; non-GAAP EPS runs ~23% above GAAP (Q1 $1.92 vs $1.56). ORCL trades at 14.6x CY2027 consensus today. Fastest EPS growth in the set (+35% FY28) stops the discount going deeper.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Legacy ~$49B revenue, 45% op margin, 20% tax = $17.6B x 15x = $264B; OCI NTM revenue ~$89B x 3.2x = $285B; less net debt ~$140B (notes + finance leases - cash, operating leases excluded); / 3.15B shares = $130

inputs_detail.value: ~$49B (Q1 FY27: software $5.55B -3%, SaaS $4.2B +10%, hardware $0.77B, services $1.41B, all x4 with SaaS growth)
inputs_detail.derivation: Q1 FY27 segment lines annualised, SaaS grown 10%
Non-GAAP op margin was 42% company-wide, with the high-margin support base above that. 15x sits between the CRM (14.3x), WDAY (14.2x) and IBM (16.8x) CY2027 P/Es.

FY28 consensus revenue $131.7B less ~$49B legacy = ~$83B OCI, and FY29 $183.6B less ~$51B = ~$132B. Blending 2/3 and 1/3 gives ~$99B, cut 10% for conversion risk. Half of the $664B RPO converts within 36 months, but only 13% within 12 months.
CRWV trades at EV $94.3B / CY2027 revenue $26.3B = 3.6x. I apply a small discount because Oracle says AI gross margins dipped during the ramp.

inputs_detail.input: Net debt at Oct-2027 (notes + finance leases - cash; operating leases excluded)
inputs_detail.derivation: Aug-26: notes $125.3B ($7.6B current + $117.7B non-current) - cash and securities $37.1B ($36.4B + $0.7B) = $88.2B, plus finance leases ~$9.2B = ~$97B (Q1 release, 10-Q). Roll to Aug-2027: Q2-Q4 FY27 FCF ~-$32 to -37B (consensus FY27 -$37B less Q1 -$5.4B; S&P says ~-$42B), Q1 FY28 ~-$8B, dividends ~$6B (0.50 x 3.02B x 4), new finance leases ~+$10B, so ~$150-155B before equity. Less the ~$18B of new equity implied by my 3.15B share count = ~$135-140B. My round-1 $170B used May-2028 consensus plus extra leases, which is too far out and double-counted. Operating-lease liabilities ($30.6B non-current) are excluded because Oracle's EBITDA is after rent.

3.000B diluted in Q1 and 3.024B outstanding at 2026-09-07 after the 141M-share, $19.9B ATM. The CY2026 plan is complete with no more bonds in CY2026; I assume ~$18B of the likely $20-40B Jan-May 2027 raise is equity at ~$145 (~125M shares, ~4%). Net debt above is net of that equity, so the two are consistent.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA at Oct-2027 = 2/3 x $74.6B + 1/3 x $107.5B = $85.6B, cut 10% to $77B, x 10x = $770B EV; less ~$140B net debt (ex operating leases); / 3.15B shares = $200

inputs_detail.derivation: Peer median CY2027 EV/EBITDA is ~15.2x (range 5.9-38x). An EBITDA-mix weighting of ~55% GPU-infrastructure (CRWV 5.9x) and ~45% software (~15x) gives ~10x, inside the range. Today ORCL trades at ~8.7x CY2027 consensus EBITDA. Peer forward EV/EBITDA figures are my own roll-forwards from trailing data, not a uniform consensus basis, so this leg gets the lowest weight (0.20).

bear.story: OpenAI (~half of RPO per S&P) slows, renegotiates or defers. RPO conversion slips and the Jupiter-type project financing (force majeure notice Sep 24, loan at 89-91c) spreads. Oracle still faces $90-95B gross capex and the Jan-May 2027 raise lands on dilutive terms. Moody's cuts to Baa3 and S&P moves back to negative outlook. EPS ~$8.5-9 at 9-10x. Net debt is lower than I assumed in round 1, so the bear price rises from $80 to $86; the S&P stable outlook lowers the junk tail slightly but the Jupiter force majeure offsets it, so the probability stays at 25%.

base.story: OCI grows triple digits as capacity comes online. FY28 revenue ~$125-130B and non-GAAP EPS ~$10-10.5 with ~4% dilution. FCF stays negative but the peak-capex message holds; the Investor Day gives margin targets without a firm FCF date. The stock holds ~14-15x NTM EPS (~$11).

bull.story: Hyperscaler 2027 capex guides come in high and OpenAI's funding de-risks the backlog (Kalshi ~50% for an IPO announcement by Jun 2027). Prepaid and bring-your-own-hardware contracts cut net capex, a dated FCF turn in FY29 emerges at the Investor Day or the June FY28 guide, and the stock re-rates to ~19-20x $12+ NTM EPS, still below the 21.5x peer median.

comps_summary.peer_range: P/E on calendar-2027 consensus non-GAAP EPS: 8.5x (ADBE) to 27.0x (NOW), n=10 (CRWV loss-making, P/E n/m, kept only as the OCI EV/sales and EV/EBITDA reference). One basis throughout: MSFT = 1/2 FY27 + 1/2 FY28; CRM and WDAY FY ending Jan-28; ADBE FY ending Nov-27; SAP on USD EPS (CY27 $9.60 @ $206.87 = 21.5x, cross-checked by the supervisor). I used Yahoo per-year estimates, not stockanalysis 'Forward PE', which mixes fiscal years. The supervisor spot-checked ADBE 8.53x, CRM 14.33x, IBM 16.7x, MSFT 24.2x and META 21.6x against my values; all match within 0.2x, so I keep my figures (IBM 16.8x and META 21.8x unchanged; differences immaterial). Sub-medians: hyperscalers 23.7x, enterprise software 15.6x. EV/CY27 EBITDA 5.9x (CRWV) to 38.1x (NOW), n=11. These are my roll-forwards of trailing EV/EBITDA at consensus growth (CRWV CY27 EBITDA ~$16B assumed), so they are a less uniform basis than the P/Es and are used as context and in a 0.20-weight leg.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: ORCL on the same basis: CY2027 EPS = 5/12 x $8.14 + 7/12 x $11.00 = $9.81, so 14.6x at $143.41 (-32% vs the 21.5x median). My 15x horizon P/E is ~30% below the median, inside the range, between CRM 14.3x and IBM 16.8x, and at the 15.6x software sub-median. My 10x EV/EBITDA is ~35% below the ~15.2x median, inside the range between CRWV 5.9x and the software peers.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount rests on company facts that persist through Oct-2027, not on sell-side calls. (a) Management calls FY27-FY28 peak capex years ($90-95B gross, up to $70B net in FY27) and on the Q1 call said it has not given a time frame for positive FCF, so FCF is negative through May 2028. (b) Funding needs ongoing: the $20B ATM (141M shares) and the ~$25B bond plus $5B mandatory convertible are done, and another $20-40B of debt or equity is likely in Jan-May 2027. (c) Credit: S&P BBB- (stable since 2026-07-09), Moody's Baa2 negative; hyperscaler peers are A or better. (d) Concentration: S&P puts ~half the $664B RPO with OpenAI, a loss-making counterparty still raising capital. (e) Earnings quality: non-GAAP EPS ~23% above GAAP (Q1 $1.92 vs $1.56), against near-GAAP hyperscaler peers. (f) The mix is shifting toward GPU leasing, which the market values at single-digit EBITDA multiples (CRWV 5.9x). Against that, ORCL has the fastest EPS growth in the set (+35% FY28 consensus), so I stay at the software sub-median rather than going lower. A move to the 21.5x median needs FCF visibility, which is my bull case.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$98 (~14% under the $114.50 52-week low, ~32% below today) the market would be pricing a fundamental break rather than volatility. That means a material OpenAI deferral or renegotiation, a funding stall (the Jan-May 2027 raise only on distressed terms, a Moody's cut plus S&P back on negative outlook, more project loans in force majeure), or a cut to the FY27 'at least $90B' revenue guide. At $98 the stock is ~10x CY2027 EPS and ~8x NTM EBITDA on ~$140B net debt, which is where my bear case sits. I keep $98: lower horizon net debt lifts my values a little, but the S&P stable outlook and the Jupiter force majeure roughly offset in the tail.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact-checks changed three of my inputs. (1) Horizon net debt: my $170B used the June-dated May-2028 consensus plus extra leases. Re-deriving from the Q1 balance sheet (notes $125.3B, cash and securities $37.1B, both verified in the 8-K) plus finance leases, Q2 FY27 to Q1 FY28 FCF, dividends and new finance leases gives ~$150-155B before equity, or ~$140B after the ~$18B of equity in my 3.15B share count. Operating leases are excluded because EBITDA is after rent. That lifts SOTP from $120 to $130 and EV/EBITDA from $190 to $200. (2) FY29: I keep my $12.6, but label it judgment ~18% below a consensus-implied ~$15.4 (my own MarketScreener ratio implies ~$16.2), so my NTM $11.0 is a ~12% haircut to consensus NTM ~$12.5. (3) The $3.3B guarantee-disappearance claim is unverified and no longer used. P/E stays at 15x NTM ($165), inside the peer range and at the software sub-median, against a 21.5x reconciled median, for the persistent reasons in comps_summary. Blend: $160 (from $154). Scenarios: bear $86 / 25%, base $158 / 50%, bull $239 / 25%. The probability-weighted mean is ~$160, which reconciles with fair value. The ladder is a lognormal mixture (medians $82/$154/$233, sigmas 0.32/0.22/0.22) with slightly fattened extreme tails. Its median is ~$154, so P(>=143) is 0.57: the mean sits above the median because of right skew, and the fat left tail is the OpenAI and funding binary. The overall spread is consistent with 56% realized vol. 1-month: centred at ~$142.9 after the dividend, sigma ~0.165 for the October Investor Day. Research this round was limited to a re-read of the Q1 release and call plus a search for the Investor Day date (not found; AI World is Oct 25-28). The Nasdaq/Zacks API was unavailable (503), so the FY29 ratio rests on the supervisor plus my MarketScreener cross-check.
